newsitem.title: USA: Venezuela official renews call for OPEC change.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela official renews call for OPEC change.

text.p: A top official at Venezuela's state oil company renewed his country's call for a change in the Organization of Petroleum Exporting Countries' (OPEC) quota system and a broadening of its role in the worldwide oil industry.

Juan Szabo, exploration and production coordinator for Petroleos de Venezuela SA (PDVSA), said OPEC needs to consider production from non-OPEC countries and the effect of increasing worldwide demand, when it sets quotas for its members.
"Everytime OPEC makes a reduction in quotas, someone else puts production on the market," he said. "Logic says if you have a growth of demand, by logic the quota system is not effective."
"Why have quotas if demand exceeds production?"
Szabo said only five or six OPEC countries currently have the capacity to exceed their quotas.

Overall, Venezuela plans to boost total domestic production to 6.3 million barrels per day in 2006 from 3.7 million barrels per day expected this year, he said. Including its share from fields operated by private companies, PDVSA will account for 4.4 million barrels per day in 2006, he said.

At the producer group's last meeting in November Venezuela proposed altering the quota system to take a producer's domestic consumption.
He said OPEC's role should be revised to include issues such as where investments in exploration and production are made throughout the world and how the industry deals with environmental issues.
"We think in Venezuela that OPEC has to broaden its agenda from just doing balances in supply and demand to taking account of other issues," he said.
He said the current quotas would not slow Venezuela's plans to boost its production in the country.
